meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 2 of 9 (quiz/game): Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides
meta.title: Echo Practice: Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A school publication's style guide says to write alumni, without an apostrophe, for all former students, regardless of gender. Which phrase follows the guide?
choices: alumni's association
alumnae association
alumni association
alumna association
questions.explanation: The phrase alumni association uses the guide's gender-inclusive plural form without an apostrophe.

questions.prompt: A school publication's guide requires Ms. with a final period when addressing a woman. Which heading follows the guide?
choices: Ms, Rivera
Ms Rivera
M.s. Rivera
Ms. Rivera
questions.explanation: Ms. Rivera follows the guide because it places a period after the abbreviation Ms.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A newspaper uses one style guide for headlines and a different one for feature articles. What is the best editing approach?
choices: Apply whichever guide gives the shorter result.
Apply the headline guide to every part of the newspaper.
Apply the feature guide to every part of the newspaper.
Apply each guide only to the section it governs.
questions.explanation: Style guides can govern different parts of a publication, and each section should be edited according to the guide that covers it.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A theater guide requires dates in numeric month/day/year format and whole numbers in descriptions to be written as words. Which program description follows both rules?
choices: The show opens on June 3, 2027 and runs for ninety minutes.
The show opens on 6/3/2027 and runs for 90 minutes.
The show opens on 3-6-2027 and runs for ninety minutes.
The show opens on 6/3/2027 and runs for ninety minutes.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the guide's numeric month/day/year date and spells out the duration in words.
questions.skill: Applying date and number style rules
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: Two equally acceptable spellings are debated within a newspaper. What should its style guide provide?
choices: A rule declaring one spelling correct for all English.
A consistent spelling rule for the newspaper.
A personal preference for each writer to follow privately.
A list of variant spellings with no recommended form.
questions.explanation: The guide should give the newspaper a shared rule so that its writers use one spelling consistently.

questions.prompt: A club's style guide says to spell out the conjunction between club names in meeting minutes and use ampersands only in the club's display name. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The Art Club & Chess Club & Drama Club held a joint meeting.
The Art Club & the Chess Club held a joint meeting.
The Art Club and the Chess Club & the Drama Club held a joint meeting.
The Art Club and the Chess Club held a joint meeting.
questions.explanation: This option spells out and between the club names as required for the meeting minutes.

questions.prompt: A community newspaper's guide says to use since for time and because for reasons. Which sentence uses both words according to those distinctions?
choices: Since the match began at noon, we missed the opening since the bus was late.
Since the match began at noon, we missed the opening because the bus was late.
Because the match began at noon, we missed the opening because the bus was late.
Because the match began at noon, we missed the opening since the bus was late.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses since to identify the time when the match began and because to identify the reason the opening was missed.
questions.skill: Applying distinctions between since and because
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: An exhibition guide requires dates in day-month-year order without ordinal suffixes. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The exhibition opens June 14 2026.
The exhibition opens 14 June 2026.
The exhibition opens 2026 June 14.
The exhibition opens 14th June 2026.
questions.explanation: The required day-month-year order with no ordinal suffix makes 14 June 2026 the compliant date.

questions.prompt: Which activity best combines echo practice with learning a house-style rule?
choices: Echo a model sentence, then identify the style choice it demonstrates.
Echo a model paragraph, then remove all its punctuation.
Read a model sentence silently, then name its main topic.
Echo a model sentence, then replace every word with a synonym.
questions.explanation: Explaining the house-style choice in an echoed model shows that the student recognized the rule as well as the pronunciation.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a style guide for a publication?
choices: To set consistent editorial rules for a publication.
To decide whether every sentence is grammatically correct.
To determine which facts an article should report.
To persuade readers to accept the writer's opinion.
questions.explanation: A style guide establishes consistent editorial conventions for a publication.
questions.skill: Identifying the purpose of a style guide

questions.prompt: A university style guide says to write the degree names bachelor's degree and master's degree in lowercase, with an apostrophe. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The program offers a bachelors degree in biology.
The program offers a Bachelor’s degree in biology.
The program offers a bachelor degree in biology.
The program offers a bachelor's degree in biology.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses the lowercase possessive form bachelor's degree exactly as the guide requires.

questions.prompt: A volunteer group's style guide says to use that for restrictive clauses and who for nonrestrictive clauses. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The volunteers who arrived before noon received the first badges.
The volunteers that arrived before noon received the first badges.
The volunteers, that arrived before noon, received the first badges.
The volunteers which arrived before noon received the first badges.
questions.explanation: The volunteers that arrived before noon restricts the group to those who arrived before noon and uses the required relative pronoun.

questions.prompt: A magazine's style guide says to lowercase the names of seasons unless they begin a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Winter enrollment usually increases after the holidays.
The team practices indoors every Winter before Spring.
The club holds a meeting in Fall and another in Spring.
Our Summer Schedule lists the Fall and Spring programs.
questions.explanation: This option correctly capitalizes Winter because it begins the sentence.

questions.prompt: A store's style guide requires fewer when referring to quantities of separate items. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: We have fewer chairs left.
We have less chairs left.
We have fewer chair left.
We have less chair left.
questions.explanation: Fewer is required for chairs because they are separate, countable items.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: Which pair of words can both be used to introduce a restrictive clause, depending on context and house style?
choices: who and whom
that and which
because and although
either and neither
questions.explanation: Both that and which can introduce a restrictive clause, although a particular style guide may prefer one.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A school's style guide says to spell out an organization's full name on first mention, followed by its abbreviation in parentheses. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration released the report.
The NASA released the report.
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) released the report.
The (NASA) National Aeronautics and Space Administration released the report.
questions.explanation: This option gives the organization's full name before introducing the abbreviation NASA in parentheses.

questions.prompt: A legal magazine's style guide says to spell out versus in running text and use vs. only in tables. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The matchup features the Hawks v. the Bears.
The matchup features the Hawks versus the Bears.
The matchup features the Hawks vs the Bears.
The matchup features the Hawks vs. the Bears.
questions.explanation: This option spells out versus in running text as the guide requires.

questions.prompt: A research center's style guide says to treat data as a plural noun and pair it with a plural verb. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The data shows a clear trend.
The data is showing a clear trend.
The data show a clear trend.
The data was showing a clear trend.
questions.explanation: This sentence pairs the plural noun data with the plural verb show.

questions.prompt: A city visitor guide says to spell out the word Avenue in full. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The center is on Oak Ave.
The center is on Oak Av.
The center is on Oak Avn.
The center is on Oak Avenue.
questions.explanation: The guide requires the street type Avenue to be written in full, so Oak Avenue is the correct form.
questions.skill: Following a house-style rule for street names
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: In choral reading practice, what do the learners do with the same passage?
choices: They read it aloud together at a shared pace.
They read separate sections aloud in sequence.
They perform it as a dialogue with invented roles.
They study its punctuation without reading aloud.
questions.explanation: Choral reading involves a group reading the same passage aloud together, usually at a coordinated pace.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: During an echo activity, the model sentence contains a disputed hyphenation. What should the learner focus on while repeating?
choices: The meaning of the hyphenated word
The exact hyphenation as shown in the model
The number of syllables in the word
The speaker's tone and pitch
questions.explanation: The learner should reproduce the exact hyphenation demonstrated in the model.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: An events guide says to use entered for entering a place or competition and entered into for joining an agreement or discussion. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: Both teams entered the tournament, and the mayor entered into the discussion.
Both teams entered into the tournament, and the mayor entered into the discussion.
Both teams entered the tournament, and the mayor entered the discussion.
Both teams entered into the tournament, and the mayor entered the discussion.
questions.explanation: It uses entered for entering the tournament and entered into for joining the discussion, as the guide requires.
questions.skill: Distinguishing similar phrases under house style
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: An online club's style guide says to use its for possession because the organization is treated as one entity. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The club changed her logo before the meeting.
The club changed it's logo before the meeting.
The club changed their logo before the meeting.
The club changed its logo before the meeting.
questions.explanation: Because the club is treated as a single entity, its is the possessive pronoun that links it to the logo.

questions.prompt: A history club's guide uses an en dash without spaces between the years in a date range. Which option follows the guide?
questions.explanation: 1920–1945 follows the guide because it places an en dash directly between the two years.
questions.skill: Applying rules for joining date ranges
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A publication's guide says to use a serial comma in lists of three or more items. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The exhibit includes paintings, and photographs and sculptures.
The exhibit includes paintings, photographs and sculptures.
The exhibit includes paintings, photographs, and sculptures.
The exhibit includes paintings and photographs, and sculptures.
questions.explanation: This sentence places a comma before the conjunction in a list of three items.

questions.prompt: A civic organization's guide requires the -ize spelling for verbs in its newsletters. Which word follows the guide?
choices: organize
organise
orginize
organze
questions.explanation: Organize follows the guide because it uses the required -ize ending.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A government report's style guide requires the abbreviation for United States to be written as U.S. with periods. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The U.S.. delegation arrived yesterday.
The US delegation arrived yesterday.
The U.S delegation arrived yesterday.
The U.S. delegation arrived yesterday.
questions.explanation: The guide mandates U.S. with periods after each letter, so the sentence using U.S. meets the requirement.

questions.prompt: Which of these is primarily a house-style rule rather than a rule of standard grammar?
choices: Use single quotation marks for short works.
Capitalize the first word of every sentence.
Form the comparative of good as better.
Place a period at the end of a complete sentence.
questions.explanation: The choice between single and double quotation marks is a publication-specific style decision rather than a core rule of grammar.

questions.prompt: A publisher's style guide says to use adviser, not advisor, in job titles. Which phrase follows the guide?
choices: senior editorial advisor
senior editorial advaiser
senior editorial adviser
senior editorial advisar
questions.explanation: The phrase uses adviser, the spelling required by the publisher's style guide.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: During echo practice, a model sentence contains a disputed punctuation choice. What should the learner do first?
choices: Read the model aloud while attending to the punctuation.
Rewrite the sentence without the disputed punctuation.
Ask classmates which punctuation they prefer.
Read the sentence silently and skip the punctuation.
questions.explanation: The learner should first read the model aloud while attending to the punctuation being practiced.
questions.skill: Echo a model while attending to a style choice

questions.prompt: An events guide says to write clock times with numerals and a.m. or p.m. and to leave one space after a period. Which sentence follows both rules?
choices: The meeting starts at 4:30 PM on Friday.
The meeting starts at 4.30 p.m. on Friday.
The meeting starts at 4:30 p.m.  on Friday.
The meeting starts at 4:30 p.m. on Friday.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the required time format, includes one space after the period, and avoids the extra space and altered formatting in the other choices.
questions.skill: Revising to match a style guide

questions.prompt: A journalism school's style guide says to use double quotation marks for a full quotation and single quotation marks for a quotation inside it. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The editor said, “Read the note marked “final” before noon.”
The editor said, ‘Read the note marked “final” before noon.’
The editor said, “Read the note marked ‘final’ before noon.”
The editor said, Read the note marked ‘final’ before noon.
questions.explanation: This option uses double quotation marks for the full quotation and single quotation marks for the quoted word inside it.

questions.prompt: An organization's style guide says to use em dashes with no spaces around them when setting off an interruption. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The final - the one we discussed - arrived late.
The final—the one we discussed—arrived late.
The final: the one we discussed: arrived late.
The final, the one we discussed, arrived late.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses em dashes without surrounding spaces to set off the interruption.

questions.prompt: During an echo activity, what should a student do immediately after hearing the model sentence?
choices: Answer a question about the model's topic instead of repeating it.
Repeat the sentence aloud, changing its meaning and word order.
Read the sentence silently while another student speaks the model.
Repeat the sentence aloud, matching the model's wording and rhythm.
questions.explanation: Echo practice involves repeating the model aloud while matching its wording, pronunciation, and rhythm.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A newsletter's style guide says to use a colon after a section label when the text after it is a complete sentence. Which version follows the guide?
choices: Contest winners: The winners being announced on Friday.
Contest winners: The judges will announce them on Friday.
Contest winners: After the judges announce them on Friday.
Contest winners: Announcing the winners on Friday.
questions.explanation: The clause The judges will announce them on Friday is a complete sentence, so the colon follows the guide.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A community newspaper's style guide says to use singular they when a person's pronouns are unknown. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The student said they would submit the report.
The student said he would submit the report.
The student said she would submit the report.
The student said he or she would submit the report.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses they without a gender-specific pronoun for a person whose pronouns are unknown.

questions.prompt: A travel publication's style guide says to use toward rather than towards. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The path leads towords the river.
The path leads towards the river.
The path leads toward the river.
The path leads towardsthe river.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses toward, the spelling required by the publication's style guide.

questions.prompt: A writing guide requires whose for possession and reserves who's for the contraction meaning who is or who has. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The author who essay won the contest received a prize.
The author who's essay won the contest received a prize.
The author whose essay won the contest received a prize.
The author whom essay won the contest received a prize.
questions.explanation: Whose is the possessive word needed to connect the author to the essay.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A columnist is writing for a magazine that uses a particular style guide, but another guide recommends a different spelling. Which choice should govern the column?
choices: The guide used by the author's school
The guide published most recently
The magazine's chosen style guide
The guide that recommends the longer spelling
questions.explanation: The publication's chosen style guide sets the house rules for the column, so the columnist should follow it.
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A museum guide requires the word through to be spelled out in captions. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The exhibit is open during September.
The exhibit is open thru September.
The exhibit is open until September.
The exhibit is open through September.
questions.explanation: The first sentence spells out through, as the museum guide requires.
questions.skill: Apply a style guide's spelling rule

questions.prompt: A publishing house's style guide says to hyphenate compound adjectives that precede a noun. Which phrase follows the guide?
choices: well-known author
well known author
well known-author
wellknown author
questions.explanation: The guide requires a hyphen between the words of a compound adjective before a noun, so well-known author is correct.

questions.prompt: A style guide must settle a disputed comma practice for its writers. Which entry would be clearest and most useful?
choices: Name the competing comma practices without recommending one.
State the preferred comma practice and show an example.
Declare the oldest practice the only acceptable form.
Choose a practice without identifying its application.
questions.explanation: A clear rule and example tell writers both what to use and how to apply it.

questions.prompt: An organization's style guide prefers active voice for its news stories. Which sentence uses active voice?
choices: The editor revised the draft.
The draft was revised by the editor.
A revision of the draft was made by the editor.
The editor's revision of the draft was made.
questions.explanation: The editor revised the draft identifies the actor in the subject position and uses the active voice.

questions.prompt: A school newspaper's style guide says to write percentages as numerals followed immediately by a percent sign. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: About thirty-five percent of students joined the club.
About 35 % of students joined the club.
About 35 percent of students joined the club.
About 35% of students joined the club.
questions.explanation: This sentence writes 35 with a numeral and places the percent sign directly after it.

questions.prompt: A newspaper's byline guide requires initials without spaces between them and a space before the surname. Which byline follows the guide?
choices: A B Chen
A.B.Chen
A.B. Chen
A. B. Chen
questions.explanation: The required format places periods after both initials and a space only before the surname.

questions.prompt: A publisher's style guide says to use numerals for exact measurements, even when they begin a sentence. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The sculpture measures 6 foot 2 inch.
The sculpture measures six feet two inches.
The sculpture measures 6 feet 2 inches.
The sculpture measures 6 feet 2 inch.
questions.explanation: The guide requires numerals for exact measurements, and 6 feet 2 inches uses a numeral with correctly pluralized unit names.

questions.prompt: A dance school's style guide uses the spelling practise for the verb meaning to rehearse. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: The dancers practice the routine twice.
The dancers practise the routine twice.
The dancers practiced the routine yesterday.
The dancers will practice the routine tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The guide uses the verb spelling practise, and that word is the verb in this sentence.
questions.skill: Applying a house-style spelling rule to a verb
questions.topic: Echo or Choral Practice - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A business magazine's style guide requires e-commerce with a hyphen and a lowercase e. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: Our e-commerce report is ready.
Our ecommerce report is ready.
Our e commerce report is ready.
Our e-commerces report is ready.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses the required hyphenated form e-commerce with a lowercase e.

questions.prompt: A newsletter's style guide says to spell out whole numbers from one through nine and use numerals for 10 and above. Which sentence follows the guide?
choices: She bought three apples and twelve oranges.
She bought 3 apples and twelve oranges.
She bought three apples and 12 oranges.
She bought 3 apples and 12 oranges.
questions.explanation: The guide requires spelling out numbers one through nine and using numerals for 10 and higher, so the sentence with three and 12 follows it.

feedback.correct: Clean strike — that's how a style guide settles it.
feedback.incorrect: That ball slipped past — a style guide would have called it.
feedback.win: Strike after strike! You argue usage like a style guide editor.
feedback.lose: The bot out-bowled you tonight. Grab a style guide and a rematch.
